role: fixed finite positive-arity relational vocabulary
notes: No constants or functions in the zero-one theorem; auxiliary names and counterexample vocabularies are separately declared.

role: labelled universe {1,...,n}
notes: n is a positive integer; differs by indexing only from the adjacent P3 convention.

role: set of labelled Y-structures
notes: Every ordered relation tuple including repetitions is independently fair.

role: cardinality of the set of labelled Y-structures
notes: 2^{sum_i k_i n^i}.

role: chosen set of isomorphism-type representatives
notes: One representative per isomorphism type; choice does not affect sentence truth.

role: number of Y-isomorphism types of size n
notes: Cardinality of B_n(Y); the unlabelled measure is uniform on these types.

role: uniform probability measure on subsets of A_n(Y)
notes: Distinct from sentence probability p_n and final-page nonuniform mixture.

role: labelled finite-model probability of a sentence
notes: Unaffected by unused relation symbols; conditional probability is separately normalized.

role: unlabelled sentence probability under uniform isomorphism types
notes: Vocabulary superscript retained since unused symbols can affect the measure.

role: complete relational open description on parameter variables
notes: No equality atoms; repeated variable tuples included; distinctness lives in axiom guards.

role: complete open description extending M by one fresh variable
notes: Retains every conjunct of M and decides every new relational atom.

role: one-point extension sentence
notes: Outer distinctness guard and fresh witness inequalities are part of the sentence.

role: theory of all relational one-point extension sentences
notes: A sentence set, not a distribution or a countable-model name.

role: number of i-ary symbols in Y
notes: Only finitely many k_i are nonzero.

role: number of fresh relational atoms involving one new point
notes: sum_i k_i((m+1)^i-m^i), including repeated entries.

role: success probability of a fixed fresh candidate extension
notes: q=2^{-d_Y(m)}; graph q=p^u(1-p)^v is separately declared in the graph theorem.

role: canonical full-relation projection-function infinite theory for spectrum proof
notes: Not the relational extension theory T; source second spectrum proof.

role: symmetry and irreflexivity conditioning sentence
notes: Conditional unrestricted binary measure equals fair simple-graph sampling.

role: tournament conditioning sentence
notes: One direction per unordered pair and no loops.

role: conditioning sentence making U uniformly true or uniformly false
notes: Conditional sentence probabilities are eventually 0, 1/2, or 1.

role: mixture mass on the full relation
notes: 0<=alpha<1; source statement-only limit claim retained.

role: auxiliary weight function for the mixed relation measure
notes: f(t)=(1-alpha)p^t+alpha.

role: fixed lower proportion used to count many nonisomorphic models
notes: 0<beta<1; unrelated to the mixture mass alpha.

role: fixed probability of an independent edge or ordered relation fact
notes: Fixed in (0,1); also used in the separately defined final-page Bernoulli mixture. Not the sentence-probability function p_n.

role: varying graph-edge probability in the boundary example
notes: p(n)=1/n^2 is outside the fixed-density graph theorem.

role: source graph predicate after replacement of unrestricted binary P
notes: An unordered-pair graph interpretation; the displayed E language is explicitly the same graph language with its edge symbol renamed.

role: sentence obtained by replacing every P atom with the corresponding Q atom
notes: Source conditional-to-graph translation preserves equality and all logical operations.

role: number 2^h of unary one-point types
notes: Not the final-page count of false ordered-pair facts.

role: number of false ordered-pair facts in one structure
notes: r+s=n^2; disjoint local role from monadic type count.

role: unique-existence abbreviation in the pairing sentences
notes: Eliminable first-order abbreviation with a fresh universally quantified comparison variable.
